question: Should OpenClaw adopt a process-wide localization runtime, including `OPENCLAW_LOCALE`, as the supported operator-facing contract for CLI and updater presentation?
rationale: The patch is a cross-surface feature series rather than a narrow bug repair; choosing its public locale-selection, fallback, and ownership model requires maintainer product and compatibility intent.

options.title: Sponsor a staged runtime contract
options.body: Approve the direction, land the foundation first, and require this slice to use public shared boundaries plus real CLI upgrade-flow proof.

options.title: Narrow to existing surface localization
options.body: Keep current surface-specific localization and defer process-wide CLI/updater locale selection until a smaller approved design is available.

options.title: Pause for RFC outcome
options.body: Keep the draft open but do not proceed until the linked localization RFC records the supported locale and compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged runtime contract
recommendation.body: Approve the direction, land the foundation first, and require this slice to use public shared boundaries plus real CLI upgrade-flow proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The updater/service handoff is a central changed user path and recent history links Vincent Koc to that area.
